description: Compare the Cse1/Cas8e L1 PAM-reading loop between the two species and check its conservation within each clade
code:
import os, json, numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from collections import Counter
OUT=os.getcwd()
exec(open(os.path.join(OUT,"alnmod.py")).read(), globals())
seqs=json.load(open(os.path.join(OUT,"cas8e_sequences.json")))
ec=seqs["ec_q46901"]
pa=None
for it in seqs["groups"]["P_aeruginosa"]:
    if "A0A3S4PYN6" in it["header"] or "WP_057392414" in it["header"]:
        pa=it["seq"]; break

ec_loop=(157,164)   # 1-based inclusive: G157..K163 -> use 157..163
pa_loop=(171,184)   # P171..K183
EC=ec[156:163]; PA=pa[170:183]
print("E. coli K-12 Cse1 L1/PAM loop 157-163 :", EC)
print("P. aeruginosa Cas8e equivalent 171-183:", PA)

# conservation of the loop across clades
def loop_cons(group, ref, lo, hi):
    out=[]
    for it in seqs["groups"][group]:
        s=it["seq"]
        p,n,sc,m = pid(ref, s)
        if p < 40: continue
        sub="".join(s[m[i]] if i in m else "-" for i in range(lo-1,hi))
        out.append(sub)
    return out

pa_loops=loop_cons("P_aeruginosa", pa, pa_loop[0], pa_loop[1]-1)
print(f"\nP. aeruginosa loop 171-183, {len(pa_loops)} sequences at >=40% id")
for s,c in Counter(pa_loops).most_common(5): print(f"   {s}  n={c}")

ec_k12=json.load(open(os.path.join(OUT,"ec_k12like_sequences.json")))
ecl=[]
for it in ec_k12["E_coli_K12like"]:
    s=it["seq"]; p,n,sc,m = pid(ec, s)
    if p<40: continue
    ecl.append("".join(s[m[i]] if i in m else "-" for i in range(156,163)))
print(f"\nE. coli K-12-like loop 157-163, {len(ecl)} sequences at >=40% id")
for s,c in Counter(ecl).most_common(5): print(f"   {s}  n={c}")

def comp(s):
    return dict(gly=sum(c=="G" for c in s), bulky=sum(c in "FWYLIVM" for c in s),
                pos=sum(c in "KR" for c in s), neg=sum(c in "DE" for c in s), n=len(s))
print("\nloop composition  E. coli:", comp(EC))
print("loop composition  P. aerug:", comp(PA))

vol=dict(G=60,A=89,S=89,C=109,D=111,P=113,N=114,T=116,E=138,V=140,Q=144,H=153,M=163,I=167,L=167,K=169,R=174,F=190,Y=194,W=228)
print(f"mean side-chain volume  E. coli loop {np.mean([vol[c] for c in EC]):.0f} A^3, "
      f"P. aeruginosa loop {np.mean([vol[c] for c in PA]):.0f} A^3")

fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.2))
for ax,(s,lab,start) in zip(axes,[(EC,"E. coli K-12 Cse1, residues 157-163",157),
                                  (PA,"P. aeruginosa Cas8e, residues 171-183",171)]):
    col=[("#2c6fbb" if c in "KR" else "#c0392b" if c in "DE" else "#e8a33d" if c in "FWYLIVM"
          else "#9aa5b1") for c in s]
    ax.bar(range(len(s)),[vol[c] for c in s],color=col,edgecolor="k",lw=0.4)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(s)))
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"{c}{start+i}" for i,c in enumerate(s)],rotation=90,fontsize=9)
    ax.set_ylim(0,200); ax.set_ylabel("side chain volume (A$^3$)"); ax.set_title(lab,fontsize=10)
fig.suptitle("The PAM-reading L1 loop of Cas8e: a glycine hinge in E. coli, a longer charged loop in P. aeruginosa\n"
             "blue = Lys/Arg, red = Asp/Glu, orange = bulky hydrophobic, grey = small polar", fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
